post_title: How many of Japan's 47 prefectures will be at the influenza warning level (≥30 cases per sentinel institution) in the MHLW weekly report for the week ending October 25, 2026?

question.title: How many of Japan's 47 prefectures will be at the influenza warning level (≥30 cases per sentinel institution) in the MHLW weekly report for the week ending October 25, 2026?
question.description:
Japan's National Epidemiological Surveillance of Infectious Diseases (NESID) tracks influenza through roughly 3,000 (formerly ~5,000) sentinel medical institutions. Each week the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) publishes "インフルエンザの発生状況について" reporting the average number of influenza patients per sentinel institution, both nationally and for each of the 47 prefectures. Two key thresholds are used: the "alert/caution level" ("注意報", 10 cases per institution) indicating a possible large outbreak within four weeks, and the "warning level" ("警報", 30 cases per institution) indicating an ongoing large outbreak.

The 2025/26 season began about a month earlier than usual. A nationwide alert was issued on October 3, 2026 — roughly a month earlier than the prior season. For the week ending October 4, 2026 (week 40), the national average was 11.35, already above the alert level of 10. Among prefectures, only Okinawa (37.07) exceeded the warning level of 30; the Tokyo metropolitan area followed with Saitama at 19.66, Chiba 18.72, Kanagawa 18.51, and Tokyo 15.87. Sixteen prefectures exceeded 10 that week. The following week (ending October 11) activity continued to spread, with many prefectures climbing toward the warning threshold.

By comparison, in the prior 2024/25-style timeline, at the equivalent calendar point in early November 2025, 25 of 47 prefectures were at or above the caution/alert level, with Miyagi, Kanagawa, and Saitama only nearing (not reaching) the ~30 warning level. The 2025/26 season running about a month ahead means several prefectures could plausibly cross the 30 warning threshold by late October 2026, though exactly how many is uncertain given week-to-week volatility and the typical mid-season acceleration.

The report covering the surveillance week of October 19–25, 2026 (2026 week 43) is expected to be published by MHLW on or about Friday, October 30, 2026. Per-prefecture weekly figures are also widely reported by Jiji Press and Nippon.com.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the number of Japan's 47 prefectures whose average reported influenza cases per sentinel medical institution ("定点当たり報告数") is 30.00 or greater for the surveillance week of October 19–25, 2026 (2026 week 43), as reported in Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) weekly influenza status release ("インフルエンザの発生状況について"), expected to be published on or about October 30, 2026. The list of weekly press releases is available at https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/kenkou_iryou/kenkou/kekkaku-kansenshou01/houdou_00023.html and per-prefecture figures at https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/seisakunitsuite/bunya/houkokusuunosuii_00007.html . The warning level ("警報") threshold is 30 cases per sentinel institution. For example, if exactly 8 prefectures report a per-sentinel average of 30.00 or higher that week, this resolves as 8.
question.fine_print: The count is based on the per-prefecture average cases per sentinel medical institution for the designated surveillance week only (not cumulative or national figures). If the MHLW figures are not published in time, the same per-prefecture weekly values as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) (e.g. Jiji Press / Nippon.com weekly flu coverage) will be used. If MHLW revises the figures, the most recent published values for that surveillance week govern. If the per-prefecture weekly data is never published anywhere, the question is annulled.
